findings.source_passage: But, though for ever mounted on that stump, never a stump-speech does the poor whaleman make; but, with downcast eyes, stands ruefully contemplating his own amputation.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'stump-speech' pun and the image of 'downcast eyes' are the rhetorical payoff of the opening anecdote; the draft loses 'for ever mounted on that stump,' 'does the poor whaleman make,' and 'with downcast eyes,' gutting the ironic comic rhythm.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence verbatim: 'But, though for ever mounted on that stump, never a stump-speech does the poor whaleman make; but, with downcast eyes, stands ruefully contemplating his own amputation.'

findings.source_passage: like the Soloma Islands, which still remain incognita, though once high-ruffed Mendanna trod them and old Figuera chronicled them.
findings.source_locator: paragraph on mountainous countries, closing simile
findings.why_it_matters: This baroque historical aside — 'high-ruffed Mendanna' and 'old Figuera' — is stylistically distinctive Melvillean erudition and thickens the passage's meditation on elusive re-discovery; the draft simply omits it.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Soloma Islands simile after 'laborious re-discovery' to preserve the characteristic voice and the interpretive weight of elusiveness.

findings.source_passage: And beneath the effulgent Antarctic skies I have boarded the Argo-Navis, and joined the chase against the starry Cetus far beyond the utmost stretch of Hydrus and the Flying Fish.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Effulgent Antarctic skies' and 'far beyond the utmost stretch of Hydrus and the Flying Fish' are the prosodic climax of the astronomical digression; the draft drops 'effulgent,' 'far beyond the utmost stretch of Hydrus and the Flying Fish,' reducing the sentence's grandeur.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'effulgent Antarctic skies' and the full closing phrase 'far beyond the utmost stretch of Hydrus and the Flying Fish' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: to see whether the fabled heavens with all their countless tents really lie encamped beyond my mortal sight!
findings.why_it_matters: The closing visionary clause — 'to see whether the fabled heavens with all their countless tents really lie encamped beyond my mortal sight' — is the rhetorical crown of the whole chapter; its excision leaves the final sentence truncated and the chapter's sublime aspiration unexpressed.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full closing clause verbatim after 'leap the topmost skies.'

summary: Three medium-severity voice-flattening losses (the stump-speech comic payoff, the Soloma Islands erudite aside, and the full Antarctic/Hydrus astronomical phrase) plus the excision of the chapter's sublime closing clause collectively degrade the segment's distinctive Melvillean register and warrant regeneration.
